answer: Across the detection horizon, bonded escrows make each identity costly to operate and expose coordinated equivocation: if k identities sign conflicting claims, the protocol aggregates evidence and scales the penalty as O(k²), rather than treating each case independently. Quill-committed proofs link the actors; upon detection, asymmetric depreciation compounds the haircut on their remaining collateral, so a sybil swarm can suffer an exponential multiplier in capital loss, not merely lose its nominal stake. No oasis of cheap identities remains.
